summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a complex history including kidney transplant with stage 4 CKD, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and pulmonary hypertension was admitted for worsening dyspnea and abdominal distension. Evaluation revealed volume overload with asymmetric pulmonary edema and elevated BNP, consistent with acute on chronic heart failure. He was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned to increased oral torsemide (100 mg QAM, 60 mg QPM). His symptoms improved, and he was euvolemic at discharge. Asymptomatic bacteriuria with Citrobacter koseri and Enterococcus was noted but not treated per transplant guidelines. Tacrolimus levels remained therapeutic. He was discharged home with optimized diuretic therapy, potassium supplementation, and plans for outpatient follow-up including a repeat CT chest in three months and echocardiogram in six months.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
